note: All configuration is the single config object protect_form_flood_control.settings (general.protect_all, general.window, general.threshold, general.protected_ids, general.unprotected_ids, general.whitelist, general.log, forms[], show_ids). Protection is enforced by attaching a validate callback that uses core's flood service (isAllowed/register). Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config object; scripts write explicit values and cleanup/reset restore the shipped install defaults (protect_all false, window 86400, threshold 50, protected_ids/unprotected_ids empty, whitelist [127.0.0.1], log false, forms {}, show_ids false).

evals.prompt: In the Drupal module Protect Form Flood Control, which config object holds the settings, and which keys define the default time window and the default maximum number of submissions per window?
evals.expected_output: The config object is protect_form_flood_control.settings. general.window (seconds) is the default flood window and general.threshold is the default max submissions per window (shipped defaults 86400 and 50).

evals.prompt: How does Protect Form Flood Control actually enforce the limit on a protected form, and what does a user see when the limit is exceeded? Which core service does it rely on?
evals.expected_output: It attaches a validate callback that calls core's flood service: flood->isAllowed(event, threshold, window). If not allowed it sets a form error ('You cannot submit the form more than N times in ...'); otherwise it registers the submission with flood->register().

evals.prompt: In Protect Form Flood Control, how do I protect every form on the site at once, and which categories of forms are always exempt from protection?
evals.expected_output: Set general.protect_all to true (protects all forms except an unprotected_ids exclusion list). Core system_*, search_* and views_exposed_form_* forms are always exempt, as is the module's own settings form.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Protect Form Flood Control's default submission threshold has been changed from the shipped value. Inspect the live protect_form_flood_control.settings config and report the current default threshold (max submissions per window).
evals.expected_output: The default threshold is 7: protect_form_flood_control.settings general.threshold = 7.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, Protect Form Flood Control has been configured to protect a specific form by its form ID (protect_all is off). Inspect the live protect_form_flood_control.settings config and report which form ID is in the protected list.
evals.expected_output: The protected form ID is user_register_form: it is listed in protect_form_flood_control.settings general.protected_ids while general.protect_all is false.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure Protect Form Flood Control to protect all forms site-wide. Apply the change to the live protect_form_flood_control.settings configuration.
evals.expected_output: protect_form_flood_control.settings general.protect_all = true (e.g. drush cset protect_form_flood_control.settings general.protect_all 1, or tick 'Protect all forms' on the settings form).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (Protect Form Flood Control is not in protect-all mode), configure it to flood-protect the site-wide contact form, whose form ID is contact_message_feedback_form, by adding it to the protected form IDs. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: protect_form_flood_control.settings general.protected_ids contains 'contact_message_feedback_form' (with general.protect_all still false).
